title: Bruno Guimaraes transfer rumours are ‘nonsense’, ‘totally disrespectful’ – Eddie Howe
content:
Eddie Howe has dismissed reports linking Bruno Guimaraes to Manchester United and Real Madrid as “nonsense” and “totally disrespectful” to Newcastle United’s captain.

Newcastle’s elimination from the Champions League at the hands of Barcelona has prompted a flurry of speculation that the club will be vulnerable to losing their best players.

Reports have stated that clubs are in talks to sign the 28-year-old midfielder, who has been sidelined since February with a hamstring injury. Howe also said Guimaraes’ midfield partner, Sandro Tonali, will be assessed before Sunday’s Tyne-Wear derby against Sunderland.

“I don’t even know how to respond to that (Guimaraes’ rumours),” Howe told reporters on Friday. “I don’t even think I should because it’s a waste of my energy. Bruno’s our captain. He’s fully committed. He’s injured at the moment. His only focus is coming back to fitness.”

With Newcastle ninth in the Premier League, seven points behind fifth-placed Liverpool, the likelihood of Howe’s team returning to the Champions League next season currently appears remote. It has led to a multitude of stories that the likes of Brazil international Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon, and Tino Livramento will seek moves elsewhere.

“Is it a problem for us? I don’t necessarily think it is a problem for us, but it is unwanted news, I suppose, is the best way to put it,” Howe said. “You don’t want the players distracted, but I don’t know how much they will absorb that.

“For me, it is not the time to think about it. In the summer, you can understand those stories a little bit more because the transfer window is open. To say our captain is in discussions with another club is totally disrespectful to Bruno more than anything else, he is totally committed here.

“I’m not going to be impolite because I don’t think it’s the forum to do that in. For me, it’s a nonsense story.”

Howe said that Guimaraes should be fit to return to fitness following the international break, but Tonali could return this weekend.  The Italy international was taken off in the 56th minute of the 7-2 loss and replaced by Joe Willock, holding his left thigh.

Howe confirmed after the game that he had a “groin or hip problem” and was a “doubt” for Sunday’s Tyne-Wear derby.

“We’ll wait and see,” Howe said on Friday when asked about the possibility of the 25-year-old playing against Sunderland. “Hopefully not as bad as maybe we first feared when I saw him limping off the pitch. We’ll see how he is today and then make a decision closer to the game.

Howe’s side are light in midfield without Guimaraes and Lewis Miley, who the head coach said this week is looking at a return towards the other end of the upcoming international break. Centre-back Fabian Schar has been out of action since undergoing surgery on an ankle injury in January.

“It’ll be after the internationals for Lewis (Miley). We anticipate he will be back, hopefully after the break. And fingers crossed the same for Bruno and also for Fabian (Schar).”
